lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: breaking a rectangle apart to show the distributive property
lessonRef.title: Concept extension: breaking a rectangle apart to show the distributive property

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example applies the idea in a new setting. Notice what stayed the same.

items.prompt: A rectangle's area is 4 × (3 + 5). Which expression shows the same area using the distributive property?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Talk through what is different about this case before you start.

items.prompt: A rectangular rug is 5 ft long and 8 ft wide. What is its area?
A rectangle 4 units long is split into two parts: one 7 units wide and one 7 units wide. Use 4 × (7 + 7) to find the total area.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A rectangle's area is 2 × (2 + 4). Which expression shows the same area using the distributive property?
A rectangular rug is 5 ft long and 7 ft wide. What is its area?
A rectangle 8 units long is split into two parts: one 5 units wide and one 3 units wide. Use 8 × (5 + 3) to find the total area.
A rectangle's area is 3 × (9 + 8). Which expression shows the same area using the distributive property?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Explain, in writing, what made this case different from the original one.

items.prompt: A rectangular rug is 7 m long and 10 m wide. What is its area?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A rectangle 7 units long is split into two parts: one 8 units wide and one 6 units wide. Use 7 × (8 + 6) to find the total area.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
